subject: Clarify SOC 2 Type II applicability across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <security@apexfin.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Eberhardt <audits@independent-audit.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II coverage question for our deployment plans

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. As we prepare our procurement and audit timeline, our audit team needs a clear statement about which Redwood-hosted artifacts are covered by your current SOC 2 Type II (period ending 2026-03-31). Specifically:

- Does the SOC 2 report cover workloads we run on Redwood Dedicated pools (reserved GPU capacity) that are provisioned and managed by Redwood for us?
- For the Private/VPC option (customer-managed control plane or on-prem package), is there any part of the SOC 2 attestation that applies, or is that fully out-of-scope unless we contract for a managed Private offering?

We also want to know what evidence (system diagrams, config snapshots, tenant isolation narrative) you can provide and whether you offer a bridge letter to cover the gap between report period and our contract start date (we expect a Feb 1, 2026 go-live).

Can you point us to a short coverage matrix and the standard attachments you can share? Our timeline: vendor selection complete 5/20, auditor kickoff 6/1.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Security, Apex Financial
security@apexfin.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <security@apexfin.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage question for our deployment plans

Hi Lena —

Thanks, great questions. Short answers up front:

- Hosted API (standard Redwood-hosted endpoints) — fully covered by our SOC 2 Type II for the report period (2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31).
- Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools) — covered when the customer is using Redwood-managed Dedicated capacity; tenant isolation and control-plane controls in scope. We provide a dedicated coverage row in the matrix.
- Private / VPC / on-prem (customer-managed control plane) — Generally out-of-scope for our standard SOC 2 unless we deliver a managed Private engagement and include it in the attestation scope. For truly customer-managed on-prem installs, we can provide a controls mapping and guidance, but the Type II report will not assert control effectiveness for the customer's own managed environment.

I'll attach a concise coverage matrix and a SOC 2 summary PDF for your auditor. We can also issue a bridge letter that explicitly states: (a) the report period, (b) that Dedicated (Redwood-managed) is covered, and (c) that customer-managed Private instances are excluded unless covered by a separate managed engagement. Bridge letters can be customized to your contract dates — we'll include the Feb 1, 2026 start date if you confirm.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_Type_II_Summary.pdf, deployments_coverage_matrix.xlsx, bridge_letter_template.docx

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll drop the matrix and summary now (attached).
2) Kimberly (security/compliance) and I can work with your auditor to map required artifacts and timelines.
3) If you want a formal bridge letter tied to Feb 1, we can provision a draft within 2 business days after you confirm the exact contract language.

Cc’ing Kimberly to coordinate evidence pulls and Ben for commercial/order details (if a managed Private engagement is being considered).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Manager, Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <security@apexfin.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage question for our deployment plans

Hi Lena, Markus —

Thanks for raising the scope nuance. A couple of clarifications from the controls/evidence side:

- For Redwood-managed Dedicated pools we can provide:
  * Tenant isolation narrative + network segmentation diagram (deployments_coverage_matrix.xlsx, tab: dedicated_isolation)
  * Sample configuration snapshots for the Dedicated control plane (redacted)
  * Service logs and uptime metrics for the report period (available on request)

- For Private/VPC (customer-managed):
  * We maintain a controls mapping (mapping of our controls to COSO/SOC 2 criteria) that shows which controls we operate vs. which controls are customer responsibilities. That mapping is useful to your auditor but does not make the Private environment itself covered by our attest report.

- Bridge letters: Our standard bridge language will state the report coverage and exclusions. If you need retroactive coverage wording that references a different report period (e.g., a backfill request), that becomes a legal/commercial conversation — happy to discuss.

Practical ask: please confirm whether Apex intends Redwood to manage the Private instance or if you will operate it yourselves. If you’ll be self-managing, we’ll put together the controls mapping and a recommended auditor-facing packet; if you want Redwood-managed Private, we’ll route to commercial to scope the managed engagement and timeline.

Attachments: deployments_coverage_matrix.xlsx (see dedicated_isolation tab)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <security@apexfin.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage question for our deployment plans

Lena — quick commercial note as you evaluate options: if Apex elects the Redwood-managed Private (we handle control plane + operational responsibilities), we can include that in scope for a future Type II cycle but it will require a managed-engagement addendum and a 60-90 day onboarding window before auditors will accept it as in-scope. If you prefer to self-manage the Private deployment, the controls mapping and sample artifacts Kimberly mentioned will generally suffice for your auditor to carve out responsibilities.

If it helps, I can set up a 30-minute call this week with our solutions engineering lead to walk through the dedicated isolation diagram and the managed private onboarding steps.

Next steps from our side: Sofia/Kimberly will prepare the bridge letter draft and the evidence packet by EOD Wed (5/6). Lena — if you confirm the desired bridge wording and whether Apex wants Redwood-managed Private, we’ll lock the language.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
